audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[4..6].side all read "Fizz" while content win[4..6] and the packet levelChart read "Anivia" — and the full-layer whys on those rows already describe Anivia taking over.
audit.why: Glacial Storm plus a mana item is where an immobile Anivia stops being divable for free; the packet chart and the content layer agree on it.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] calls Chum the Waters a "stun-into-burst kill".
audit.why: Chum the Waters knocks up the attached target and knocks nearby enemies aside — it is a displacement, not a stun, thrown from 1300 range on a 120/100/80s cooldown. Calling it a stun hides both the range and the once-every-two-minutes cost.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and enemyWin now name the knockup and the 1300 range.
sources: enemyKit R text, range and cd

audit.whatIsWrong: Every interaction line reduces to "the untargetable hop dodges your combo", with no cooldown attached, and two real interactions are absent entirely: Nimble Fighter's flat damage reduction and Seastone Trident's auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Playful/Trickster is 16 seconds at rank 1 — that is the punish window and the page never says the number. Nimble Fighter cuts a flat amount off every damage source, which specifically taxes Anivia's chip poke. Seastone Trident is an auto reset, so the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the ability cast. Urchin Strike is a 550 dash and Crystallize is terrain: his passive moves him through units, not through ice, so the wall genuinely stops the engage.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, ahead, the do/don't details and the early paragraph now carry the 16s window, the flat damage reduction, the auto-reset tell and the terrain-versus-dash point.

audit.why: Both suspectNames entries are false positives: "Chum the Waters" is Fizz's real R and "Glacial Storm" is Anivia's real R, named in Riot's own Frostbite text.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Crystallize has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Playful/Trickster is 16s at rank 1 and it eats your whole combo untargetable — bait the hop, then Flash Frost while it is down. - Seastone Trident is an auto reset: the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. - Crystallize is for the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: Fizz wins by landing Playful / Trickster, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Fizz wins by hopping over your stun untargetable, landing Chum the Waters from 1300, and killing bird and egg.

edits.before: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Fizz away from the comeback farm, and rotate first to every river fight with your stun loaded.
edits.after: Ahead, price the dive: storm every wave, wall Urchin Strike off the catch-up farm, and fight only while Playful/Trickster is on cooldown.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the hop — Playful/Trickster is 16 seconds at rank 1, and Frostbite doubles on anything the storm has chilled.

edits.before: The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Sixteen seconds at rank 1 — bait the hop with a step toward the wave, then spend Flash Frost into the landing, never into the air.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Fizz burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Urchin Strike is a 550 dash and Crystallize is terrain — his passive walks through units, not through ice, so the wall still cuts the engage.

edits.before: Fizz whiffs Playful / Trickster and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Chum the Waters reaches 1300 — tower is the only place it is not free.

edits.before: That is Fizz’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Nimble Fighter cuts flat damage from every source — chip poke does less than you think.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Crystallize is 17s and it is the only thing that stops Urchin Strike — never spend it on spacing.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Fizz walks straight at you.
edits.after: He is untargetable through the whole hop and his passive walks him through your minions — the chase is never yours.

edits.before: Your Glacial Storm zone finally punishes his dive windows even though Chum the Waters still threatens a stun-into-burst kill.
edits.after: Your Glacial Storm finally punishes his dive windows, but Chum the Waters knocks you up from 1300 into the full combo.

edits.before: Fizz's Seastone Trident poke and untargetable Playful/Trickster dashes let him harass you freely at levels 1-2 while dodging your slow, telegraphed Q entirely, so trades heavily favor him early. He can dive in for damage and hop right back out before you can punish. Play from max range, ward for his jungle-side roams, and avoid overcommitting Q since whiffing just gives him a free window to poke you down.
edits.after: Fizz's Seastone Trident poke and untargetable Playful/Trickster let him harass freely at levels 1-2 while dodging your slow, telegraphed Q, and Nimble Fighter shaves a flat amount off every source of damage you own, so your chip lands smaller than it looks. Play from max range, ward his jungle-side roams, and never overcommit Q — a whiff gives him a free window to poke you down.

notes: Level chart: win[4..6] already read "Anivia" on disk, so only the three full-layer side tokens are proposed; both layers agree after the write. Fizz's R is flagged projectile/blockable by Wind Wall-class effects, but Crystallize is terrain rather than a projectile wall, so I did not claim it blocks Chum the Waters. Whether the fish can be body-blocked by minions is not in Riot's text and was not asserted.
